g.text: outside the file and its tests
Whyline’s record lives beside your code as git notes.
You run git push as usual.
The pre-push hook sends the notes to origin too.
Your teammate pulls and merges payments-v2.
Post-merge fetches the notes, then runs whyline check.
Two items are now due, including the mock gateway.
No server, no dependencies: the record travels with the code.
Two real PRs on the demo shop. PR #1 removes the mock gateway.
It fetches the notes and installs whyline from GitHub.
Nothing is past its condition, so the check passes.
PR #2 leaves the mock gateway behind.
No references left: exit 2, error on the file.
The condition Whyline recorded for the mock is now a gate.
In the Whyline repo, every push to main runs pages.yml.
It rebuilds the demo from recorded sessions and runs whyline report.
One offline HTML page, six views, live on GitHub Pages.
AI bill of materials: 49 of 96 lines AI-written, 7 Bob sessions.
In a live Bob IDE run, cost comes from Bob’s task DB.
47 unreviewed AI lines, with test coverage shown when a report exists.
Proposed Team tier: an org admin sets Bob’s EnforcedHooks policy once.
Every developer’s Bob would then run the four whyline hooks.
With whyline init in each repo, notes land beside the code.
Proposed: one dashboard across the org’s repos.
Proposed: each release keeps its report as a compliance record.
The MIT CLI, skills and dashboard stay free.
